newsitem.title: USA: Miami hosts record 9.6 million tourists in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Miami hosts record 9.6 million tourists in 1996.

text.p: A record 9.6 million tourists visited the Miami area in 1996, topping the previous year's record total by 2.1 percent, the Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau said Wednesday.
Tourist spending also set a record, climbing 29 percent over 1995 to $10.9 billion in 1996, the bureau said.
The domestic market grew by 3.3 percent to 4.5 million visitors, while the international market increased by one percent to 5.1 million.

Bureau President Merrett Stierheim said visitor polling showed the highest satisfaction rates since the bureau started tracking in 1989, with 88 percent of overnight visitors saying they were extremely or very satisfied and 79 percent saying they were likely to return.

The international market is expected to show continued growth from Europe, led by the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Italy in 1997. European visitors totaled 1.3 million in 1996, the highest number in a decade.

Tourism from Canada and South America remains strong, while Mexico's fluctuating economy and a series of economically devastating hurricanes has reduced toursim from Central America and the Caribbean, the bureau said.
In the domestic market, researchers expect steady growth from the South, although the Northeast still represents the largest domestic market share.
The data are for all of Dade County, which includes the Miami urban area and Miami Beach.
